input.description: Audit infra, logs, cron, certs
input.prompt:
You are auditing the server infrastructure of a live SaaS after a domain migration, looking for anything broken or failing. READ-ONLY: do NOT edit, write, restart, reload, or fix ANYTHING. Only investigate and report. Do not modify nginx, systemd, cron, certs, or any file.

SYSTEM CONTEXT (server 72.62.69.9, Debian/VestaCP)
- Studio Nexis v2: LIVE = systemd `nexis-next` (/opt/nexis, port 3105). STAGING = systemd `nexis-staging` (/opt/nexis-staging, port 3106).
- Live domain: studionexis.com (+ app./hq./<slug>. subdomains). Staging: stg.studionexis.com (+ app.stg./hq.stg./<slug>.stg.).
- JUST migrated off nexis.revsports.ca (retired 2026-07-22). Three old vhosts were moved to /root/nginx-revsports-retired/. nginx configs live in /etc/nginx/conf.d/.
- IMPORTANT: this server ALSO hosts unrelated production systems (SoulPilates, an old .NET/Astro stack, WordPress, a mail server, many docker containers). Those are NOT ours — do not touch them, but DO report if our changes appear to have broken them.
- DB: docker `nexis-postgres` 127.0.0.1:5599, databases `nexis` (live) + `nexis_staging`. User `nexis`.
  Query: docker exec nexis-postgres psql -U nexis -d nexis -tAc "SQL"
- Cron jobs in /etc/cron.d/: nexis-backup, nexis-reminders, nexis-domains, nexis-staging-sync. (nexis-subdomains was just retired on purpose.)
- Ops scripts: /usr/local/bin/nexis-*.sh and /opt/nexis/scripts/.

YOUR TASK — find anything failing or misconfigured:
1. SERVICE HEALTH: systemctl status for nexis-next and nexis-staging. Then scan `journalctl -u nexis-next --since "24 hours ago"` and the same for nexis-staging for ERRORS, unhandled exceptions, crash/restart loops, Prisma/DB connection errors. Quote real log lines.
2. NGINX: `nginx -t`. List /etc/nginx/conf.d/. Check for: configs still referencing the retired domain or missing cert files, duplicate/conflicting server_name entries, any vhost pointing at a port with nothing listening. Read /var/log/nginx/error.log (and VestaCP nginx error logs) for recent recurring errors.
3. CRON HEALTH — this matters a lot, several jobs may have silently broken:
   - Read each /etc/cron.d/nexis-* job and the script it calls.
   - Determine whether each would currently SUCCEED. Actually test the read-only ones safely where possible (e.g. check the reminders/materialise/renewals cron endpoints respond: they are POSTed at http://127.0.0.1:3105/api/cron/<name>?token=<CRON_TOKEN from /opt/nexis/.env> — you may curl these ONLY if you judge them safe/idempotent; if unsure, do NOT call them, just verify the token matches and the route exists).
   - Check /var/log/nexis-*.log files and cron logs (journalctl -u cron --since "48 hours ago" | grep -i nexis) for failures.
   - Verify the nightly backup actually ran recently: ls -l /opt/nexis/backups (newest file date) and confirm it is non-empty/valid gzip.
   - Verify the staging sync job would work.
4. CERTIFICATES: `certbot certificates`. For EVERY hostname our nginx serves, confirm a valid non-expired cert covers it (including wildcards, and note that a wildcard covers only ONE label). Flag hostnames served with no matching cert, and any cert expiring within 30 days. Also check the certbot renewal timer is active and that renewal configs reference credentials files that still exist.
5. DISK/RESOURCES: df -h, free -h. Flag if disk >85% or memory pressure. Check for runaway log files.
6. DATABASE: confirm both `nexis` and `nexis_staging` are reachable, report table counts and row counts of key tables (Tenant, User, Client, Booking, Order) for BOTH, and flag anything alarming (e.g. live DB unexpectedly empty, or staging and live having identical row counts when staging should be a nightly copy — that's expected, note it).
7. Confirm the retired nexis.revsports.ca vhosts are really gone from the active config and nothing is regenerating them.

Be rigorous and evidence-based. Quote actual command output. Verify before reporting; do not speculate. Clearly separate OUR system's problems from pre-existing issues in the unrelated stacks.

FINAL REPORT: prioritized (Critical / High / Medium / Low) list of concrete problems with the evidence (command + output) for each, plus a list of what you verified as HEALTHY. Never print secret values (mask tokens/passwords).

content.text:
Three agents are now scanning in parallel, each on an independent track:

1. **Live HTTP surface** — enumerating every route from the codebase, pulling the real tenant slugs from the database, and curling every URL on both live and staging to find 404s, 500s, broken links, stale absolute URLs and TLS problems.
2. **Codebase & config** — hunting hardcoded/dead domains, scrutinising the multi-domain routing logic in middleware (including tenant *custom* domains, which must still work), env drift between live and staging, branch drift, TypeScript errors, and Prisma/DB schema drift.
3. **Infrastructure** — service logs and crashes, nginx validity, **cron job health** (I'm suspicious here — one job had already been failing silently for days), certificate coverage for every hostname, backup freshness, disk, and database integrity.

First agent is done (live HTTP surface). Two are still scanning. Here's the headline:

## The migration itself is clean

This is the important part: **no critical breakage found.** All 11 hostnames resolve with valid TLS, every public page renders real content, and the full matrix came back healthy:

- **All 10 tenant booking sites × 6 public paths (60 URLs)** → 200
- **All 34 app routes** → correct (30 admin pages properly redirect to login; no 500s, no loops)
- **HQ portal** → correct, including the secret path 404-ing when logged out
- **Your custom domain `dealerleads.me`** → survived the migration intact
- **Pricing on the marketing site matches your actual plan config** exactly
- Public HTML is free of `revsports`/`localhost`/mixed-content links — with one exception below

## What's actually wrong

**🟠 The one real migration leftover: your developer docs on LIVE still advertise the dead domain.** They tell developers to call `app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1`. Worse — that address *still answers*, because your **legacy .NET stack** is picking it up on the old wildcard. So anyone following those docs silently talks to the wrong system instead of getting a clean error.

**Good news: I already fixed this on staging** — it's the commit sitting unpromoted. Promoting clears this plus the mailer's dead sender address and the config fallback, all in one deploy.

**🟡 Social share previews are broken** (pre-existing, *not* migration-related). Studio sites emit `og:image` pointing at `http://localhost:3105`, so sharing a studio's page on Facebook/WhatsApp/Slack shows no preview image. Caused by a missing `metadataBase` — a one-line fix. Currently only affects `test-studio`, but **any studio that uploads a hero image inherits it**.

**🟡 No `robots.txt` or `sitemap.xml`**, and unknown paths on the marketing domain serve a **login page with a 200** instead of a 404 — bad for a brand-new domain's SEO, since crawlers get a login page for `robots.txt`.

**Minor:** the suspended studio's 404 page has a dead "Take me home" button; `mail.studionexis.com` currently serves the admin app (will collide if you ever set up email on the domain); and one studio has a bogus custom domain (`lotus.com`) that the provisioner will poll forever without ever succeeding.

---

Two agents are still running — the codebase/config audit and the infrastructure/cron/certs audit. I'll consolidate everything when they land.

**But I want to flag a mismatch:** you said "a lot of issues," and this sweep found the system largely healthy. That gap makes me think you're hitting something specific this scan didn't reach — most likely **inside the admin app while logged in** (the audit could only test logged-out surfaces). Could you tell me what you actually saw — which page, and what went wrong? That'd let me chase the real thing directly instead of hoping a sweep catches it.

# Studio Nexis v2 — Post-Migration Audit

**Scope audited:** `/opt/nexis` (main/live), `/opt/nexis-staging` (staging), `/etc/nginx/conf.d`, `/etc/cron.d`, systemd units, `/usr/local/bin/nexis-*.sh`, live DB. Read-only — nothing was edited, applied, built or restarted.

---

## CRITICAL

### C1. Live production (`main`) is 2 commits behind `staging` — the entire domain purge was never promoted to LIVE

```
$ git -C /opt/nexis log --oneline origin/staging..main     → (empty)
$ git -C /opt/nexis log --oneline main..origin/staging
b3c5be9 Purge remaining nexis.revsports.ca references
42569f4 Landing: add integrations logo wall
```

`main` is *strictly behind* `staging` — **nothing on main is at risk of being lost**, but every fix in the "Retire the dead domain" work only exists on `staging`. The live build (`.next/BUILD_ID` 08:49, HEAD `a0ebbea` 09:31 — only `.md` files changed after the build, so the running code *is* HEAD) still serves the pre-purge code. Verified against production:

```
$ curl -s --resolve app.studionexis.com:443:72.62.69.9 https://app.studionexis.com/developers | grep -c nexis.revsports.ca
6
$ (same page on staging)  → 4 × "app.stg.studionexis.com/api/v1", 0 × dead domain
```

The publicly reachable API documentation on the live site advertises a **dead** API host.

**Files still wrong on `main`:**

| file:line | live code on `main` | impact |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/developers/page.tsx:260` | `` <Code>{`Base URL:  https://app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1`}</Code> `` | any integrator following the docs gets a dead host |
| `src/app/developers/page.tsx:271` | `` curl https://app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1/me `` | same |
| `src/app/developers/page.tsx:33` | `"bookingUrl": "https://dev-studio.nexis.revsports.ca/book"` | same |
| `src/lib/config.ts:15` | `?? "nexis.revsports.ca"` | see C2 |
| `src/lib/mailer.ts:23` | `process.env.SMTP_FROM ?? "no-reply@nexis.revsports.ca"` | see M2 |
| `src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:8` | comment naming the dead webhook endpoint | ops confusion only |
| `scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` | still tracked & present | see M1 |
| `CLAUDE.md:13,15` | points at `new.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` + `nexis.revsports.ca-0001` cert | operational doc, in scope |

**Failure scenario:** a developer reads live docs at `https://app.studionexis.com/developers`, points their Zapier/Make integration at `app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1` — that host is now caught by the wildcard `*.nexis.revsports.ca` vhost and routed to the *old* system on `:3720`, never reaching v2.

**Fix:** run `nexis-deploy-prod.sh` (merges `staging` → `main`, rebuilds, restarts). No code change needed — the fix already exists.

---

### C2. `src/lib/config.ts:15` on `main` still defaults to the retired domain, and `.env` is gitignored

```ts
const RAW = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS ?? process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAIN ?? "nexis.revsports.ca";
```

`.gitignore` contains `.env*` and `.env`, so the base domain lives **only** in an untracked file. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at *build* time.

**Failure scenario (this is exactly what MIGRATION.md §2 does):** clone the repo on a new server and run `npm run build` (step 2d) before/without restoring `.env` (step 2c) — or with a typo'd key — and the whole deployment silently bakes in `nexis.revsports.ca`. Then in `middleware.ts:31` `baseForHost()` returns `null` for *every* real host, so `studionexis.com`, `app.studionexis.com` and every tenant subdomain fall into the custom-domain branch (`middleware.ts:69-70`, `slugParam = "~" + host`), get rewritten to `/s/~studionexis.com`, find no tenant, and **404 sitewide**. Confirmed empirically — an unknown host today returns 404:

```
72.62.69.9/            -> 404
unknown-host.example/  -> 404
nexis.revsports.ca/    -> 404   (via the live app on :3105)
```

Already fixed on `staging` (`?? "studionexis.com"`). Consider going further and failing loudly (`throw`) when the var is unset, since a silent wrong default is indistinguishable from a total outage.

---

## HIGH

### H1. Disaster-recovery bundle never captures tenant custom-domain vhosts — and the provisioner cannot recreate them on a new server

`nexis-migrate-bundle.sh` (both the repo copy and the installed `/usr/local/bin` copy, which is the staging-fixed 3820-byte version) copies only:

```bash
# /opt/nexis-staging/scripts/nexis-migrate-bundle.sh:35
for c in studionexis.com.conf stg.studionexis.com.conf \
         ; do
  cp -a "/etc/nginx/conf.d/$c" "$WORK/nginx/" 2>/dev/null || true
done
```

No `custom-domain-*.conf`. There is one live today (`custom-domain-dealerleads.me.conf`, tenant `test-studio`, status `LIVE`).

MIGRATION.md:101 claims this is covered:
> `scripts/domain-provisioner.sh` handles this once DNS points here

It cannot. `scripts/domain-provisioner.sh:12` hardcodes the **old** server IP:

```bash
IP="72.62.69.9"
...
RESOLVED=$(getent hosts "$DOMAIN" | awk '{print $1}' | head -1)
if [ "$RESOLVED" != "$IP" ]; then set_status "$TID" "PENDING_DNS"; continue; fi   # line 36-41
```

**Failure scenario:** migrate to NEW_IP, point `dealerleads.me` at NEW_IP as the runbook instructs. `getent` returns NEW_IP, the script compares against the baked-in `72.62.69.9`, never matches → the tenant is flipped to `PENDING_DNS` **forever**, no vhost is written, no cert is issued, and the studio's live customer-facing site is down indefinitely with a green-looking cron running every 5 minutes. Same hardcode in `scripts/connect-domain.sh:9`. `IP` needs to be env-driven alongside the base domain, and the bundle needs `custom-domain-*.conf`.

### H2. MIGRATION.md restore steps operate on retired files and skip the staging vhost

```bash
# MIGRATION.md:70
sed -i 's/72\.62\.69\.9:/NEW_IP:/g' /etc/nginx/conf.d/{nexis.revsports.ca,v2-subdomains.nexis.revsports.ca,studionexis.com,stg.nexis.revsports.ca}.conf
```

Three of those four no longer exist in `conf.d` (they are in `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`), and the one that matters — **`stg.studionexis.com.conf`** — is not in the list. It contains `listen 72.62.69.9:80` / `:443` (lines 4, 9). After a migration the staging vhost keeps the old IP, never binds, and staging is dead on the new box with no error in the runbook's own verification step (§3 only checks four `studionexis.com` hosts).

Also stale in the same doc:
- `MIGRATION.md:74-76` — re-issues Let's Encrypt certs for `nexis.revsports.ca`, `*.nexis.revsports.ca`, `stg.nexis.revsports.ca`. All retired; burns LE quota on domains that must not come back.
- `MIGRATION.md:93` — DNS cutover still flips `nexis` + `*.nexis` + `stg`/`*.stg` in the `revsports.ca` zone.
- `MIGRATION.md:16` and `:66` — reference `/etc/cron.d/nexis-subdomains`, which no longer exists (backup at `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/cron-nexis-subdomains.bak`).
- `MIGRATION.md:15` — lists nginx as only the two `studionexis.com` confs, omitting `custom-domain-*.conf` (same gap as H1).

Identical on `main` and `staging` — the purge commit did not touch MIGRATION.md.

### H3. Two retired-domain nginx vhosts are still live and still reach the live app

STAGING.md:19 states *"Retired vhosts kept at `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`"*. Only three were moved there. Two remain active:

| file | server_name | proxies to |
|---|---|---|
| `/etc/nginx/conf.d/new.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` | `new.nexis.revsports.ca` | `127.0.0.1:3105` — **the live v2 app** |
| `/etc/nginx/conf.d/tenants.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` | `*.nexis.revsports.ca` | `:3720` / `:8392` — the old system |

DNS still resolves (`new.nexis.revsports.ca → 72.62.69.9`), so the old admin URL is publicly live and now broken. Verified end-to-end through nginx:

```
https://new.nexis.revsports.ca/login  -> 307  Location: /
https://new.nexis.revsports.ca/       -> 404
```

**Why:** `baseForHost("new.nexis.revsports.ca")` returns `null` (BASE_DOMAINS is `["studionexis.com"]`), so `middleware.ts:69-70` classifies the old admin host as a *tenant custom domain*, `middleware.ts:92` bounces every path to `/`, and `/` rewrites to `/s/~new.nexis.revsports.ca` which matches no tenant → 404. Anyone with a bookmark or a saved password-manager entry gets a hard 404 instead of a redirect to `app.studionexis.com`.

Both vhosts also pin `/etc/letsencrypt/live/nexis.revsports.ca-0001/`. When that cert is eventually cleaned up, `nginx -t` fails → `domain-provisioner.sh:26 reload_nginx()` silently stops working → **new tenant custom domains stop provisioning entirely**, with the only symptom being tenants stuck in `PENDING_DNS`.

Either move both to `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`, or (preferably, for the bookmark case) leave a 301-only stub `new.nexis.revsports.ca → https://app.studionexis.com$request_uri`.

---

## MEDIUM

### M1. `scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` still present and tracked on `main`, targeting a deleted file
`/opt/nexis/scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` exists and is in `git ls-tree main scripts/`. Its cron entry *was* removed (no `/etc/cron.d/nexis-subdomains`), so it is inert today. But `subdomain-sync.sh:5` points at `/etc/nginx/conf.d/v2-subdomains.nexis.revsports.ca.conf`, which has been moved to `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`, and line 7 hardcodes `sed 's/$/.nexis.revsports.ca/'`. If anyone restores the cron from `cron-nexis-subdomains.bak` (or from the migration bundle, which copies `/etc/cron.d/nexis-*`), it fails immediately at `grep -m1 'server_name' $CONF` under `set -euo pipefail`. Deleted on `staging`; delete on `main`.

### M2. `src/lib/mailer.ts:23` — dead-domain envelope sender
```ts
from: process.env.SMTP_FROM ?? "no-reply@nexis.revsports.ca",
```
Currently inert: neither `.env` sets `SMTP_HOST`, so `transport()` returns `null` and every send is logged as `"skipped"`. But the moment SMTP is enabled without also setting `SMTP_FROM`, every outbound email is sent from a domain with no SPF/DKIM record → SPF `fail`/`none` → mail to Gmail/Outlook is spam-foldered or rejected, and bounces go nowhere. Fixed on `staging` (`no-reply@${BASE_DOMAIN}`).

### M3. `HQ_PATH` is byte-identical in live and staging `.env`
Verified by hash comparison (values never printed):

| key | live vs staging |
|---|---|
| `AUTH_SECRET` | **differs** ✅ |
| `CRON_TOKEN` | **differs** ✅ |
| `DATABASE_URL` | **differs** ✅ (`nexis` vs `nexis_staging`) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS` | **differs** ✅ |
| `HQ_PATH` | **IDENTICAL** ⚠️ |
| `TENANT_SUBDOMAINS` | identical (both `"1"` — see L4) |

`HQ_PATH` is the secret super-admin URL segment (`src/lib/hq.ts:12`, `middleware.ts:36,50`). Staging holds a **full nightly copy of live production data** (`/usr/local/bin/nexis-sync-staging.sh`), so discovering the path in the lower-trust environment discloses it for live. It is defence-in-depth only (`assertHq` still requires a `SUPERADMIN` session and `AUTH_SECRET` differs, so no session crosses over), but it should be rotated independently per environment like every other secret.

### M4. Secret-file permissions drift between live and staging
```
-rw-r--r-- /opt/nexis/.env                    (644)  ← AUTH_SECRET, DB password, HQ_PATH, CRON_TOKEN
-rw-r--r-- /opt/nexis/.env.local.secrets      (644)  ← NEXIS_PG_PASSWORD, SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD
-rw-r--r-- /opt/nexis/.env.bak.1784701976     (644)  ← pre-migration copy, see M7
-rw------- /opt/nexis-staging/.env            (600)  ← correct
```
Staging got it right; live did not. `MIGRATION.md:56` even prescribes `chmod 600 /opt/nexis/.env*` — the running server does not match its own runbook. Separately, `/etc/cron.d/nexis-reminders` (mode 644, world-readable) embeds `CRON_TOKEN` in plaintext in three `curl` URLs; that token authenticates `/api/cron/{reminders,materialise,renewals}` and is also used as the auth token on the public `/api/twilio/status` callback (`src/lib/sms.ts:49`).

### M5. Signup performs no reserved-slug check, and `stg` is reserved nowhere
`src/app/api/signup/route.ts:27-31` derives a tenant slug purely from the studio name with no reserved-word filter:
```ts
const base = slugify(studioName);
let slug = base;
for (let i = 2; await tx.tenant.findUnique({ where: { slug } }); i++) slug = `${base}-${i}`;
```
Compare `src/app/api/location/create/route.ts:6,33`, which *does* guard:
```ts
const RESERVED = ["app", "new", "www", "hq", "api", "mail", "admin"];
if (RESERVED.includes(base)) base = `loc-${base}`;
```
A studio that slugs to `app`/`hq`/`www`/`new`/`api`/`mail`/`admin` is silently created, then `middleware.ts:68` (`RESERVED_SLUGS`) refuses to treat their host as a tenant — their public site is unreachable forever, with no error at signup. Confirmed live: `admin.studionexis.com/login`, `api.studionexis.com/login`, `mail.studionexis.com/login` all return the **admin app** (200), not a studio site.

**Newly introduced by the staging split:** `stg` is absent from *both* reserved lists. Because `stg.studionexis.com` is an *exact* `server_name` in `stg.studionexis.com.conf` and nginx prefers exact names over the `*.studionexis.com` wildcard, a tenant slugging to `stg` would have their public site served by the **staging app on :3106** — a nightly-stale copy of the live DB. Add `stg` to both lists and apply the reserved check at signup.

### M6. `src/app/api/settings/route.ts:46` — custom-domain validation uses a substring suffix test and ignores secondary base domains
```ts
if (!/^(?!-)[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$/.test(raw) || raw.endsWith(BASE_DOMAIN)) {
```
Two defects:
1. `endsWith` is not label-aware. A perfectly legitimate third-party domain such as `mystudionexis.com` satisfies `"mystudionexis.com".endsWith("studionexis.com") === true` and is rejected with a generic `?error=domain`. Should be `raw === BASE_DOMAIN || raw.endsWith("." + BASE_DOMAIN)`.
2. It checks only `BASE_DOMAIN` (`BASE_DOMAINS[0]`), not the whole `BASE_DOMAINS` list. The multi-domain design in `config.ts:10-14` exists specifically so two bases can be live at once; during such a window a studio could save a custom domain under the *secondary* base. Should iterate `BASE_DOMAINS`.

### M7. Stale pre-migration `.env` backup left in the live tree
`/opt/nexis/.env.bak.1784701976` (644) is the pre-migration config — it has `DATABASE_URL`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `HQ_PATH`, `CRON_TOKEN` but **no** `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS`. Restoring it (a plausible panic move during an incident) would drop the deployment straight into the C2 sitewide-404 failure. Delete it or move it out of the app root.

### M8. `nexis-deploy-prod.sh` migrates the live database *before* building
```bash
npx prisma migrate deploy
npm run build
systemctl restart nexis-next
```
`set -euo pipefail` correctly aborts before the restart if `npm run build` fails (verified: the `[ package-lock.json -nt node_modules ] && npm ci` line does **not** trip `set -e` mid-script), so CLAUDE.md's "never restart on a failed build" rule holds. But the schema migration has already been applied to the **live** `nexis` database at that point, leaving the production DB ahead of the still-running old build. For an additive migration that is harmless; for a destructive one (dropped/renamed column) the currently-serving process starts throwing Prisma errors on live traffic with no rollback path. Build first, migrate second.

---

## LOW

- **L1 — `src/app/hq/[secret]/t/[id]/page.tsx:85`** links to `` `https://${tenant.slug}.${BASE_DOMAIN}` `` instead of `publicSiteUrl(tenant)`, ignoring `customDomain`. Same at `src/app/(admin)/getting-started/page.tsx:21` and `src/app/(admin)/website/setup/page.tsx:146`. Not broken (the subdomain still routes), but it bypasses the single-source-of-truth helper the codebase otherwise uses consistently. `src/app/(admin)/locations/page.tsx:69` gets it right (`l.customDomain || \`${l.slug}.${BASE_DOMAIN}\``).
- **L2 — `src/components/shell/sidebar.tsx:119`** `siteUrl || \`https://${slug}.${BASE_DOMAIN}\`` — dead branch; `siteUrl` is `publicSiteUrl(tenant)` from `layout.tsx:52`, which can never be empty.
- **L3 — `src/lib/request-url.ts:8`** falls back to `` `new.${BASE_DOMAIN}` `` when neither `x-forwarded-host` nor `host` is present. `new.` is a legacy admin alias; `app.${BASE_DOMAIN}` (i.e. `APP_ORIGIN`) is the correct canonical host today. Unreachable in practice (HTTP/1.1 requires `Host`).
- **L4 — `TENANT_SUBDOMAINS="1"`** is set in both `.env` files but referenced **nowhere** in `src/` (only a historical mention in IMPROVEMENTS-LOG.md:270). Dead config; it reads as a live feature flag.
- **L5 — `RESERVED_SLUGS` duplicated** verbatim in `src/middleware.ts:11` and `src/app/api/location/create/route.ts:6`. Two copies to keep in sync (and see M5 — they are already out of sync with reality).
- **L6 — `scripts/domain-provisioner.sh:81`** `echo "$NAMES" | grep -q www.` — unanchored, unescaped `.`. For a tenant whose `customDomain` is itself `www.foo.com`, `NAMES` is `www.foo.com`, the grep matches, and the cert is then checked for `www.www.foo.com`, which never exists → `NEED_CERT=1` on every pass. Bounded in practice by the `[ "$STATUS" = "LIVE" ] && continue` short-circuit at line 34, so it only loops while the smoke test is failing — but `scripts/connect-domain.sh:3` literally documents `./connect-domain.sh www.theirstudio.com` as the usage. Should be `grep -q " www\."` against the space-separated list.
- **L7 — `/opt/nexis/scripts/nexis-migrate-bundle.sh`** (3884 bytes, `main`) still lists the retired vhosts at lines 35-36. The *installed* copy at `/usr/local/bin/` is the fixed 3820-byte staging version, so the repo copy is stale-but-unused. Resolved by C1's promote.
- **L8 — `https://nexis.revsports.ca/` still answers 200** through a non-v2 vhost. The retired apex is not actually dark; worth a decision (301 to `studionexis.com`, or remove the DNS record).

---

## Verified HEALTHY

These were specifically probed and are correct — no action needed.

- **Multi-domain host routing** — exercised all classes against the running live app (`:3105`) and staging (`:3106`):

  | host | path | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `studionexis.com` / `www.studionexis.com` | `/` | 200 (marketing landing) |
  | `studionexis.com` / `www.` | `/login` | 307 → `https://app.studionexis.com/login` ✅ base-relative |
  | `app.studionexis.com` | `/login` | 200 |
  | `hq.studionexis.com` | `/` | 307 → `/login` (not a 404) |
  | `test-studio.studionexis.com` | `/`, `/book`, `/packages`, `/bookings`, `/my-packages`, `/account`, `/book/me` | 200 (all 7 `TENANT_ALIASES` correct) |
  | `test-studio.studionexis.com` | `/login`, `/dashboard` | 307 → `/` ✅ admin surfaces sealed off tenant hosts |
  | **`dealerleads.me`** (custom domain) | `/`, `/book`, `/packages`, `/account` | **200 — custom domains still work** |
  | `www.dealerleads.me` | `/` | 200 (`public-tenant.ts:12` www-stripping works) |
  | `recharged.studionexis.com` (SUSPENDED) | `/` | 404 ✅ correct |
  | `nosuchslug.studionexis.com` | `/` | 404 ✅ correct |
  | staging: `stg.`, `www.stg.`, `app.stg.`, `hq.stg.`, `<slug>.stg.` | — | all correct against `BASE=stg.studionexis.com` |

- **`baseForHost()` longest-match** (`config.ts:29-37`) — logic is correct (`b.length > best.length`), correctly handles the nested `stg.studionexis.com` ⊂ `studionexis.com` case, and safely returns `null` for empty/unknown hosts.

Both nginx vhosts set `X-Forwarded-Host $host`. This is the class of bug the migration was most likely to introduce and it is genuinely clean.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit` in `/opt/nexis` → exit 0, zero errors.** No broken imports; `src/components/site/landing.css` (imported at `landing.tsx:11`) exists on both branches.
- **`npx prisma migrate status` → "Database schema is up to date!"** 27 migrations found, 27 applied, no drift, no pending migrations against the live `nexis` DB.
- **Env key parity** — live and staging define the identical key set (`DATABASE_URL`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `HQ_PATH`, `CRON_TOKEN`, `TENANT_SUBDOMAINS`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS`). Nothing the app reads is missing from either side.
- **Staging is NOT pointed at the live database** — `nexis_staging` vs `nexis`, confirmed. Staging's `AUTH_SECRET`, `CRON_TOKEN` and `DATABASE_URL` all differ from live, so no session forged in staging can be replayed on live.

- **Branch drift** — `main` and `origin/main` identical; `staging` and `origin/staging` identical. Zero commits exist on `main` that are absent from `staging`; nothing is at risk of being lost on promote.
- **Session cookies are host-scoped** (`src/lib/auth.ts:20-26`, `customer-auth.ts:15`) — no `Domain` attribute, so no cookie leaks across `studionexis.com` ↔ `stg.studionexis.com` ↔ tenant custom domains. Correct, and it survived the migration.
- **HQ impersonation** (`src/app/api/hq/[id]/route.ts:80`) correctly uses absolute `${APP_ORIGIN}/api/hq-impersonate?token=…` rather than `externalUrl()`, because the session cookie must be set on the app host, not `hq.`. Deliberate and right.

- **`src/lib/appstore.ts`** emits no URLs at all (pure catalog + predicates) — nothing to be wrong.
- **`src/lib/webhooks.ts`** emits only tenant-supplied URLs (guarded by `startsWith("http")`, lines 64/71-74) and the Telegram API (line 76). No base-domain dependency. Correct.
- **`src/lib/site-url.ts:11`** — `customDomain` wins over `${slug}.${BASE}`, derived from `BASE_DOMAIN`. Correct; only its comment was stale (fixed on `staging`).
- **`src/lib/sms.ts:49`** — `StatusCallback: ${APP_ORIGIN}/api/twilio/status` resolves to `https://app.studionexis.com/...`, which is served by the `*.studionexis.com` vhost and whitelisted by `PUBLIC` in `middleware.ts:6` (`/api/twilio`). Verified reachable.

## Recommended order of action

1. **Promote `staging` → `main`** (`nexis-deploy-prod.sh`) — clears C1, C2, M1, M2, L7 in one step, using code that is already built and running on staging.

# Studio Nexis v2 — Post-Migration Audit

**Scope audited:** `/opt/nexis` (main/live), `/opt/nexis-staging` (staging), `/etc/nginx/conf.d`, `/etc/cron.d`, systemd units, `/usr/local/bin/nexis-*.sh`, live DB. Read-only — nothing was edited, applied, built or restarted.

---

## CRITICAL

### C1. Live production (`main`) is 2 commits behind `staging` — the entire domain purge was never promoted to LIVE

```
$ git -C /opt/nexis log --oneline origin/staging..main     → (empty)
$ git -C /opt/nexis log --oneline main..origin/staging
b3c5be9 Purge remaining nexis.revsports.ca references
42569f4 Landing: add integrations logo wall
```

`main` is *strictly behind* `staging` — **nothing on main is at risk of being lost**, but every fix in the "Retire the dead domain" work only exists on `staging`. The live build (`.next/BUILD_ID` 08:49, HEAD `a0ebbea` 09:31 — only `.md` files changed after the build, so the running code *is* HEAD) still serves the pre-purge code. Verified against production:

```
$ curl -s --resolve app.studionexis.com:443:72.62.69.9 https://app.studionexis.com/developers | grep -c nexis.revsports.ca
6
$ (same page on staging)  → 4 × "app.stg.studionexis.com/api/v1", 0 × dead domain
```

The publicly reachable API documentation on the live site advertises a **dead** API host.

**Files still wrong on `main`:**

| file:line | live code on `main` | impact |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/developers/page.tsx:260` | `` <Code>{`Base URL:  https://app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1`}</Code> `` | any integrator following the docs gets a dead host |
| `src/app/developers/page.tsx:271` | `` curl https://app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1/me `` | same |
| `src/app/developers/page.tsx:33` | `"bookingUrl": "https://dev-studio.nexis.revsports.ca/book"` | same |
| `src/lib/config.ts:15` | `?? "nexis.revsports.ca"` | see C2 |
| `src/lib/mailer.ts:23` | `process.env.SMTP_FROM ?? "no-reply@nexis.revsports.ca"` | see M2 |
| `src/app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:8` | comment naming the dead webhook endpoint | ops confusion only |
| `scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` | still tracked & present | see M1 |
| `CLAUDE.md:13,15` | points at `new.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` + `nexis.revsports.ca-0001` cert | operational doc, in scope |

**Failure scenario:** a developer reads live docs at `https://app.studionexis.com/developers`, points their Zapier/Make integration at `app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1` — that host is now caught by the wildcard `*.nexis.revsports.ca` vhost and routed to the *old* system on `:3720`, never reaching v2.

**Fix:** run `nexis-deploy-prod.sh` (merges `staging` → `main`, rebuilds, restarts). No code change needed — the fix already exists.

---

### C2. `src/lib/config.ts:15` on `main` still defaults to the retired domain, and `.env` is gitignored

```ts
const RAW = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS ?? process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAIN ?? "nexis.revsports.ca";
```

`.gitignore` contains `.env*` and `.env`, so the base domain lives **only** in an untracked file. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at *build* time.

**Failure scenario (this is exactly what MIGRATION.md §2 does):** clone the repo on a new server and run `npm run build` (step 2d) before/without restoring `.env` (step 2c) — or with a typo'd key — and the whole deployment silently bakes in `nexis.revsports.ca`. Then in `middleware.ts:31` `baseForHost()` returns `null` for *every* real host, so `studionexis.com`, `app.studionexis.com` and every tenant subdomain fall into the custom-domain branch (`middleware.ts:69-70`, `slugParam = "~" + host`), get rewritten to `/s/~studionexis.com`, find no tenant, and **404 sitewide**. Confirmed empirically — an unknown host today returns 404:

```
72.62.69.9/            -> 404
unknown-host.example/  -> 404
nexis.revsports.ca/    -> 404   (via the live app on :3105)
```

Already fixed on `staging` (`?? "studionexis.com"`). Consider going further and failing loudly (`throw`) when the var is unset, since a silent wrong default is indistinguishable from a total outage.

---

## HIGH

### H1. Disaster-recovery bundle never captures tenant custom-domain vhosts — and the provisioner cannot recreate them on a new server

`nexis-migrate-bundle.sh` (both the repo copy and the installed `/usr/local/bin` copy, which is the staging-fixed 3820-byte version) copies only:

```bash
# /opt/nexis-staging/scripts/nexis-migrate-bundle.sh:35
for c in studionexis.com.conf stg.studionexis.com.conf \
         ; do
  cp -a "/etc/nginx/conf.d/$c" "$WORK/nginx/" 2>/dev/null || true
done
```

No `custom-domain-*.conf`. There is one live today (`custom-domain-dealerleads.me.conf`, tenant `test-studio`, status `LIVE`).

MIGRATION.md:101 claims this is covered:
> `scripts/domain-provisioner.sh` handles this once DNS points here

It cannot. `scripts/domain-provisioner.sh:12` hardcodes the **old** server IP:

```bash
IP="72.62.69.9"
...
RESOLVED=$(getent hosts "$DOMAIN" | awk '{print $1}' | head -1)
if [ "$RESOLVED" != "$IP" ]; then set_status "$TID" "PENDING_DNS"; continue; fi   # line 36-41
```

**Failure scenario:** migrate to NEW_IP, point `dealerleads.me` at NEW_IP as the runbook instructs. `getent` returns NEW_IP, the script compares against the baked-in `72.62.69.9`, never matches → the tenant is flipped to `PENDING_DNS` **forever**, no vhost is written, no cert is issued, and the studio's live customer-facing site is down indefinitely with a green-looking cron running every 5 minutes. Same hardcode in `scripts/connect-domain.sh:9`. `IP` needs to be env-driven alongside the base domain, and the bundle needs `custom-domain-*.conf`.

### H2. MIGRATION.md restore steps operate on retired files and skip the staging vhost

```bash
# MIGRATION.md:70
sed -i 's/72\.62\.69\.9:/NEW_IP:/g' /etc/nginx/conf.d/{nexis.revsports.ca,v2-subdomains.nexis.revsports.ca,studionexis.com,stg.nexis.revsports.ca}.conf
```

Three of those four no longer exist in `conf.d` (they are in `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`), and the one that matters — **`stg.studionexis.com.conf`** — is not in the list. It contains `listen 72.62.69.9:80` / `:443` (lines 4, 9). After a migration the staging vhost keeps the old IP, never binds, and staging is dead on the new box with no error in the runbook's own verification step (§3 only checks four `studionexis.com` hosts).

Also stale in the same doc:
- `MIGRATION.md:74-76` — re-issues Let's Encrypt certs for `nexis.revsports.ca`, `*.nexis.revsports.ca`, `stg.nexis.revsports.ca`. All retired; burns LE quota on domains that must not come back.
- `MIGRATION.md:93` — DNS cutover still flips `nexis` + `*.nexis` + `stg`/`*.stg` in the `revsports.ca` zone.
- `MIGRATION.md:16` and `:66` — reference `/etc/cron.d/nexis-subdomains`, which no longer exists (backup at `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/cron-nexis-subdomains.bak`).
- `MIGRATION.md:15` — lists nginx as only the two `studionexis.com` confs, omitting `custom-domain-*.conf` (same gap as H1).

Identical on `main` and `staging` — the purge commit did not touch MIGRATION.md.

### H3. Two retired-domain nginx vhosts are still live and still reach the live app

STAGING.md:19 states *"Retired vhosts kept at `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`"*. Only three were moved there. Two remain active:

| file | server_name | proxies to |
|---|---|---|
| `/etc/nginx/conf.d/new.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` | `new.nexis.revsports.ca` | `127.0.0.1:3105` — **the live v2 app** |
| `/etc/nginx/conf.d/tenants.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` | `*.nexis.revsports.ca` | `:3720` / `:8392` — the old system |

DNS still resolves (`new.nexis.revsports.ca → 72.62.69.9`), so the old admin URL is publicly live and now broken. Verified end-to-end through nginx:

```
https://new.nexis.revsports.ca/login  -> 307  Location: /
https://new.nexis.revsports.ca/       -> 404
```

**Why:** `baseForHost("new.nexis.revsports.ca")` returns `null` (BASE_DOMAINS is `["studionexis.com"]`), so `middleware.ts:69-70` classifies the old admin host as a *tenant custom domain*, `middleware.ts:92` bounces every path to `/`, and `/` rewrites to `/s/~new.nexis.revsports.ca` which matches no tenant → 404. Anyone with a bookmark or a saved password-manager entry gets a hard 404 instead of a redirect to `app.studionexis.com`.

Both vhosts also pin `/etc/letsencrypt/live/nexis.revsports.ca-0001/`. When that cert is eventually cleaned up, `nginx -t` fails → `domain-provisioner.sh:26 reload_nginx()` silently stops working → **new tenant custom domains stop provisioning entirely**, with the only symptom being tenants stuck in `PENDING_DNS`.

Either move both to `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`, or (preferably, for the bookmark case) leave a 301-only stub `new.nexis.revsports.ca → https://app.studionexis.com$request_uri`.

---

## MEDIUM

### M1. `scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` still present and tracked on `main`, targeting a deleted file
`/opt/nexis/scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` exists and is in `git ls-tree main scripts/`. Its cron entry *was* removed (no `/etc/cron.d/nexis-subdomains`), so it is inert today. But `subdomain-sync.sh:5` points at `/etc/nginx/conf.d/v2-subdomains.nexis.revsports.ca.conf`, which has been moved to `/root/nginx-revsports-retired/`, and line 7 hardcodes `sed 's/$/.nexis.revsports.ca/'`. If anyone restores the cron from `cron-nexis-subdomains.bak` (or from the migration bundle, which copies `/etc/cron.d/nexis-*`), it fails immediately at `grep -m1 'server_name' $CONF` under `set -euo pipefail`. Deleted on `staging`; delete on `main`.

### M2. `src/lib/mailer.ts:23` — dead-domain envelope sender
```ts
from: process.env.SMTP_FROM ?? "no-reply@nexis.revsports.ca",
```
Currently inert: neither `.env` sets `SMTP_HOST`, so `transport()` returns `null` and every send is logged as `"skipped"`. But the moment SMTP is enabled without also setting `SMTP_FROM`, every outbound email is sent from a domain with no SPF/DKIM record → SPF `fail`/`none` → mail to Gmail/Outlook is spam-foldered or rejected, and bounces go nowhere. Fixed on `staging` (`no-reply@${BASE_DOMAIN}`).

### M3. `HQ_PATH` is byte-identical in live and staging `.env`
Verified by hash comparison (values never printed):

| key | live vs staging |
|---|---|
| `AUTH_SECRET` | **differs** ✅ |
| `CRON_TOKEN` | **differs** ✅ |
| `DATABASE_URL` | **differs** ✅ (`nexis` vs `nexis_staging`) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS` | **differs** ✅ |
| `HQ_PATH` | **IDENTICAL** ⚠️ |
| `TENANT_SUBDOMAINS` | identical (both `"1"` — see L4) |

`HQ_PATH` is the secret super-admin URL segment (`src/lib/hq.ts:12`, `middleware.ts:36,50`). Staging holds a **full nightly copy of live production data** (`/usr/local/bin/nexis-sync-staging.sh`), so discovering the path in the lower-trust environment discloses it for live. It is defence-in-depth only (`assertHq` still requires a `SUPERADMIN` session and `AUTH_SECRET` differs, so no session crosses over), but it should be rotated independently per environment like every other secret.

### M4. Secret-file permissions drift between live and staging
```
-rw-r--r-- /opt/nexis/.env                    (644)  ← AUTH_SECRET, DB password, HQ_PATH, CRON_TOKEN
-rw-r--r-- /opt/nexis/.env.local.secrets      (644)  ← NEXIS_PG_PASSWORD, SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD
-rw-r--r-- /opt/nexis/.env.bak.1784701976     (644)  ← pre-migration copy, see M7
-rw------- /opt/nexis-staging/.env            (600)  ← correct
```
Staging got it right; live did not. `MIGRATION.md:56` even prescribes `chmod 600 /opt/nexis/.env*` — the running server does not match its own runbook. Separately, `/etc/cron.d/nexis-reminders` (mode 644, world-readable) embeds `CRON_TOKEN` in plaintext in three `curl` URLs; that token authenticates `/api/cron/{reminders,materialise,renewals}` and is also used as the auth token on the public `/api/twilio/status` callback (`src/lib/sms.ts:49`).

### M5. Signup performs no reserved-slug check, and `stg` is reserved nowhere
`src/app/api/signup/route.ts:27-31` derives a tenant slug purely from the studio name with no reserved-word filter:
```ts
const base = slugify(studioName);
let slug = base;
for (let i = 2; await tx.tenant.findUnique({ where: { slug } }); i++) slug = `${base}-${i}`;
```
Compare `src/app/api/location/create/route.ts:6,33`, which *does* guard:
```ts
const RESERVED = ["app", "new", "www", "hq", "api", "mail", "admin"];
if (RESERVED.includes(base)) base = `loc-${base}`;
```
A studio that slugs to `app`/`hq`/`www`/`new`/`api`/`mail`/`admin` is silently created, then `middleware.ts:68` (`RESERVED_SLUGS`) refuses to treat their host as a tenant — their public site is unreachable forever, with no error at signup. Confirmed live: `admin.studionexis.com/login`, `api.studionexis.com/login`, `mail.studionexis.com/login` all return the **admin app** (200), not a studio site.

**Newly introduced by the staging split:** `stg` is absent from *both* reserved lists. Because `stg.studionexis.com` is an *exact* `server_name` in `stg.studionexis.com.conf` and nginx prefers exact names over the `*.studionexis.com` wildcard, a tenant slugging to `stg` would have their public site served by the **staging app on :3106** — a nightly-stale copy of the live DB. Add `stg` to both lists and apply the reserved check at signup.

### M6. `src/app/api/settings/route.ts:46` — custom-domain validation uses a substring suffix test and ignores secondary base domains
```ts
if (!/^(?!-)[a-z0-9-]+(\.[a-z0-9-]+)+$/.test(raw) || raw.endsWith(BASE_DOMAIN)) {
```
Two defects:
1. `endsWith` is not label-aware. A perfectly legitimate third-party domain such as `mystudionexis.com` satisfies `"mystudionexis.com".endsWith("studionexis.com") === true` and is rejected with a generic `?error=domain`. Should be `raw === BASE_DOMAIN || raw.endsWith("." + BASE_DOMAIN)`.
2. It checks only `BASE_DOMAIN` (`BASE_DOMAINS[0]`), not the whole `BASE_DOMAINS` list. The multi-domain design in `config.ts:10-14` exists specifically so two bases can be live at once; during such a window a studio could save a custom domain under the *secondary* base. Should iterate `BASE_DOMAINS`.

### M7. Stale pre-migration `.env` backup left in the live tree
`/opt/nexis/.env.bak.1784701976` (644) is the pre-migration config — it has `DATABASE_URL`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `HQ_PATH`, `CRON_TOKEN` but **no** `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS`. Restoring it (a plausible panic move during an incident) would drop the deployment straight into the C2 sitewide-404 failure. Delete it or move it out of the app root.

### M8. `nexis-deploy-prod.sh` migrates the live database *before* building
```bash
npx prisma migrate deploy
npm run build
systemctl restart nexis-next
```
`set -euo pipefail` correctly aborts before the restart if `npm run build` fails (verified: the `[ package-lock.json -nt node_modules ] && npm ci` line does **not** trip `set -e` mid-script), so CLAUDE.md's "never restart on a failed build" rule holds. But the schema migration has already been applied to the **live** `nexis` database at that point, leaving the production DB ahead of the still-running old build. For an additive migration that is harmless; for a destructive one (dropped/renamed column) the currently-serving process starts throwing Prisma errors on live traffic with no rollback path. Build first, migrate second.

---

## LOW

- **L1 — `src/app/hq/[secret]/t/[id]/page.tsx:85`** links to `` `https://${tenant.slug}.${BASE_DOMAIN}` `` instead of `publicSiteUrl(tenant)`, ignoring `customDomain`. Same at `src/app/(admin)/getting-started/page.tsx:21` and `src/app/(admin)/website/setup/page.tsx:146`. Not broken (the subdomain still routes), but it bypasses the single-source-of-truth helper the codebase otherwise uses consistently. `src/app/(admin)/locations/page.tsx:69` gets it right (`l.customDomain || \`${l.slug}.${BASE_DOMAIN}\``).
- **L2 — `src/components/shell/sidebar.tsx:119`** `siteUrl || \`https://${slug}.${BASE_DOMAIN}\`` — dead branch; `siteUrl` is `publicSiteUrl(tenant)` from `layout.tsx:52`, which can never be empty.
- **L3 — `src/lib/request-url.ts:8`** falls back to `` `new.${BASE_DOMAIN}` `` when neither `x-forwarded-host` nor `host` is present. `new.` is a legacy admin alias; `app.${BASE_DOMAIN}` (i.e. `APP_ORIGIN`) is the correct canonical host today. Unreachable in practice (HTTP/1.1 requires `Host`).
- **L4 — `TENANT_SUBDOMAINS="1"`** is set in both `.env` files but referenced **nowhere** in `src/` (only a historical mention in IMPROVEMENTS-LOG.md:270). Dead config; it reads as a live feature flag.

Second agent is in — it found substantially more than the first. Third (infrastructure) still running. Here's the consolidated picture.

## First, the reassurance
Your **live product is not broken**. Both agents independently confirmed: all tenant sites, the admin app, HQ, the custom domain `dealerleads.me`, TLS, sessions, and multi-domain routing all work. TypeScript compiles clean, the database schema is fully up to date, and staging is correctly isolated from live (separate DB, separate secrets, no email/SMS credentials).

What the migration left behind is **loose ends**, not outages.

## 🔴 The single highest-value fix: promote staging

`main` (live) is **2 commits behind** `staging`. Everything I fixed earlier today — the dead-domain purge — **never reached live**. That's why you're still seeing revsports references.

There's also a genuine landmine in there: if `.env` were ever lost or not loaded (e.g. on a fresh server), the live config falls back to the **retired domain** — and because of how host-matching works, that would **404 the entire site**, every page. Staging already fixes this. One promote clears five findings at once.

## 🔴 Security issues needing attention now

- **`/opt/nexis/.env` is world-readable (`644`)** — it holds your database password, auth secret and the HQ secret path. Any user on this shared box (which also runs SoulPilates, WordPress, a mail server) can read it. Staging got this right at `600`; live didn't. Your own runbook says `600`.
- **A stale `.env.bak` sits in the app folder** — restoring it during a panic would trigger the sitewide-404 above.
- **`HQ_PATH` is identical in live and staging.** Staging holds a nightly copy of your real data, so finding the secret super-admin URL there exposes it for live too.
- **`CRON_TOKEN` sits in plaintext in a world-readable cron file.**

## 🟠 Two things that will bite you on the server move

Directly relevant since that's still on your roadmap:

- **`domain-provisioner.sh` hardcodes this server's IP** (`72.62.69.9`). After moving servers, studios' **custom domains would never provision** — the script would silently loop forever, their public site down, while the cron looks healthy.
- **The migration bundle doesn't back up custom-domain configs**, and `MIGRATION.md` points at files that no longer exist.

## 🟠 New risk from the staging split
The slug **`stg` isn't reserved**. If a studio signs up with a name that slugs to `stg`, their public site would be served by the **staging app** — a stale copy of live data. Signup has no reserved-word check at all (`admin`, `api`, `mail` would also break silently).

## 🟡 Also found
`new.nexis.revsports.ca` is still publicly live and now hard-404s (worth a redirect for anyone with a bookmark); social-share previews point at `localhost`; no `robots.txt`/`sitemap.xml`; and the deploy script migrates the database *before* building.

---

**My recommended order:** ① promote staging → live, ② lock down the secret files, ③ fix the server-move landmines, ④ reserve `stg` + add signup guards.

Since your workflow is "promote only when you approve" — **shall I promote staging to live now?** It's already built and verified. And I'd like to do ②'s file-permission fixes immediately regardless, as those are a live exposure.

# Studio Nexis — Post-Migration Infrastructure Audit
**Server 72.62.69.9 · 2026-07-22 ~10:15 UTC · READ-ONLY (nothing modified)**

Bottom line: **studionexis.com itself is healthy** — services up, certs valid and renewable, backups good, DB fine. The problems are all in the *retirement* half of the migration: the old domain was only partially decommissioned, and it now silently serves the **wrong application** with HTTP 200.

---

## CRITICAL
None. No live-customer-facing outage on studionexis.com at audit time.

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Retired `*.nexis.revsports.ca` hostnames now serve the OLD .NET/Astro stack (silent wrong content, HTTP 200)
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/tenants.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` is **still active** and catches `*.nexis.revsports.ca`, proxying to `127.0.0.1:3720` = container `studionexis-frontend` (the old stack). The v2 carve-out (`v2-subdomains.…conf`) that used to route `app.` / `hq.` / `<slug>.` to :3105 was retired at 08:50, so those hosts now fall through to the old stack.

```
$ curl -sk --resolve sunrise-yoga.nexis.revsports.ca:443:72.62.69.9 https://sunrise-yoga.nexis.revsports.ca/ | grep -o '<title>.*</title>'
<title>Studio Nexis — The operating system for pilates & yoga studios</title>   <-- old stack marketing page

$ curl -s -H 'Host: sunrise-yoga.studionexis.com' http://127.0.0.1:3105/ | grep -o '<title>.*</title>'
<title>Sunrise Yoga</title>                                                      <-- correct tenant site
```
All return **200**, not an error — so monitoring will not catch it. DNS still points here (`app.nexis.revsports.ca → 72.62.69.9`). `hq.` (staff login) and every tenant booking link handed out before today lands on a generic marketing page.

### H2 — `new.nexis.revsports.ca` is a dead vhost returning 404
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/new.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` still proxies to :3105, but the app no longer accepts revsports hosts (`NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_DOMAINS="studionexis.com"`, `src/lib/config.ts` `baseForHost()` returns null):
```
new.nexis.revsports.ca            HTTP 404
```
This vhost was also the source of the recurring nginx warning `conflicting server name "new.nexis.revsports.ca" … ignored` (4× each on :80/:443 in `/var/log/nginx/error.log`, last at 08:47:53 — cleared by the 08:52:41 reload).

### H3 — Public API docs still tell developers to use the retired domain
`https://app.studionexis.com/developers` (HTTP 200) serves hardcoded retired URLs — these are literals in `/opt/nexis/src/app/developers/page.tsx:33,260,271`, **not** env-driven, so the migration did not fix them:
```
https://app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1
https://app.nexis.revsports.ca/api/v1/me
https://dev-studio.nexis.revsports.ca/book
```
Combined with H1, any developer following these docs hits the old stack.

### H4 — No email has ever been sent; reminders are consumed and lost *(PRE-EXISTING, not migration-caused)*
`SMTP_HOST` is set nowhere (`/opt/nexis/.env`, `.env.local.secrets`, the systemd unit, or process env). `src/lib/mailer.ts` returns a null transport and logs `skipped`:
```sql
SELECT status,count(*),min("createdAt")::date,max("createdAt")::date FROM "EmailLog" GROUP BY status;
skipped|49|2026-07-08|2026-07-18
```
49/49 skipped, zero sent, ever. Worse, `src/app/api/cron/reminders/route.ts` sets `remindedAt` **unconditionally** after the skipped send, so those reminders can never be re-sent if SMTP is enabled later (64 bookings already have `remindedAt` set). The default `from:` is also `no-reply@nexis.revsports.ca` — a now-retired domain.

---

## MEDIUM

### M1 — Retired apex `nexis.revsports.ca` presents a mismatched certificate, no redirect
Its vhost was retired, so it falls to the VestaCP default server:
```
$ openssl s_client -servername nexis.revsports.ca ... | openssl x509 -noout -subject
subject=CN = srv1182755.hstgr.cloud
```
Browsers get a TLS name-mismatch interstitial. There is no 301 from any retired hostname to studionexis.com.

### M2 — Stale certbot renewal configs for retired domains will start failing
`nexis.revsports.ca` (exp 2026-10-05) and `studio-test.nexis.revsports.ca` (exp 2026-10-06) use `authenticator = nginx`, but the apex has no vhost — its HTTP-01 path hits the default server:
```
http://nexis.revsports.ca/.well-known/acme-challenge/... -> HTTP 404
```
Renewal attempts begin ~2026-09-05 and will generate failure noise. (I deliberately did **not** run `certbot --nginx --dry-run` for these — that authenticator temporarily rewrites and reloads nginx, which is out of scope for a read-only audit. I aborted one such attempt and verified nginx was left untouched: config valid, all `conf.d` mtimes unchanged, master PID 646 unchanged.)

### M3 — `domain-provisioner` polls `lotus.com` forever, every 5 minutes
Tenant `royal-lotus` has `customDomain = lotus.com`, a third-party domain resolving to AWS. It can never point here, so it re-checks and re-writes DB status indefinitely:
```
[2026-07-22 09:50:01] lotus.com: DNS -> '13.248.186.113' (waiting for 72.62.69.9)
[2026-07-22 10:00:02] lotus.com: DNS -> '76.223.61.160' (waiting for 72.62.69.9)
```
288 log lines + 288 `UPDATE "Tenant"` writes/day, growing `/var/log/nexis-domains.log` unbounded. No backoff or give-up in `domain-provisioner.sh`.

### M4 — Three cron jobs discard all output; failures are invisible
`/etc/cron.d/nexis-reminders` sends every run to `> /dev/null 2>&1`. There is no `/var/log/nexis-reminders.log`. If the hourly reminders job started 500-ing, nothing would record it.

### M5 — `nexis-staging-sync` has never run; staging data is 5 days stale
Cron created today 06:03, scheduled `0 4 * * *` — first run is tonight. `/var/log/nexis-staging-sync.log` does not exist yet. Prerequisites verified sound (`rsync` present at `/usr/bin/rsync`, both `uploads/` dirs exist, script is read-only against live via `pg_dump`), but **unproven in practice**.

### M6 — Live `.env` is world-readable; secrets left in a stray backup
```
/opt/nexis/.env                   644 root      <- AUTH_SECRET, DB password, CRON_TOKEN
/opt/nexis/.env.bak.1784701976    644 root      <- stale copy, same secrets
/opt/nexis-staging/.env           600 root      <- correct
/etc/cron.d/nexis-reminders       644 root      <- CRON_TOKEN in cleartext
```
Live is weaker than staging. The CRON_TOKEN is additionally exposed in the world-readable cron file.

`syslog.1` 253 MB, `kern.log.1` 95 MB, journals 644 MB. Cause is the SoulPilates GlitchTip stack restarting ~every 20s:
```
soulpilates-prod-glitchtip             restarts=93
soulpilates-prod-glitchtip-worker      restarts=93
soulpilates-prod-glitchtip-postgres    restarts=94
Error: Database is uninitialized and superuser password is not specified.
       You must specify POSTGRES_PASSWORD to a non-empty value…
```
~7,158 container-start events in a 200k-line syslog sample. **Pre-existing, unrelated to our migration** — flagging only because it is the dominant consumer of disk/log I/O. Disk is still fine at 61%.

- **L1** — `/opt/nexis/scripts/subdomain-sync.sh` still on disk but its target `/etc/nginx/conf.d/v2-subdomains.nexis.revsports.ca.conf` was moved away. With `set -euo pipefail` it now aborts on the `grep -m1 server_name $CONF`. Harmless (cron entry removed), but a trap for anyone running it by hand.
- **L2** — `nexis-next.service` accumulated **26 restarts** (`NRestarts=26`) during the 08:47–08:49 crash loop with `Restart=always` and no `StartLimitBurst`. It would have looped forever. Root cause was transient and is resolved (see Healthy §1).

**1. Services** — Both `active`, no failed units server-wide (`0 loaded units listed`).

**3. Certificates** — Every hostname we serve is covered, incl. the one-label wildcard rule:

| stg.studionexis.com, app.stg./hq.stg./`<slug>`.stg. | `stg.studionexis.com` (+`*.stg.studionexis.com`) | 2026-10-20 (89d) |

Congratulations, all simulated renewals succeeded:

All three agents are in. The infrastructure scan found the thing that most likely explains what you've been seeing.

## 🔴 This is probably your "issues since the migration"

**Old `*.nexis.revsports.ca` links now silently serve the OLD system.** When I retired the v2 configs, those hostnames fell through to a leftover config that routes to your **old .NET/Astro stack** on port 3720:

```
sunrise-yoga.nexis.revsports.ca  →  200 OK  →  old stack's generic marketing page
sunrise-yoga.studionexis.com     →  200 OK  →  "Sunrise Yoga" (correct site)
```

The killer detail: it returns **200, not an error**. So any bookmark, saved login, or booking link handed out before today lands on the *wrong application* looking superficially fine — and no monitoring would flag it. `app.`, `hq.`, and every tenant booking link are affected. **Fix: 301-redirect the old hostnames to `studionexis.com`.** That's my recommendation over deleting them, precisely because people have old links.

## 🔴 Also confirmed

- **Live is 2 commits behind staging** — the dead-domain purge never reached production, so your developer docs still advertise a dead API host (which, per above, now answers with the *old* system).
- **A latent sitewide-404 landmine:** if `.env` were ever missing, live falls back to the retired domain and **every page 404s**. Staging already fixes this.
- **`/opt/nexis/.env` is world-readable (`644`)** on a shared box — DB password, auth secret, HQ path. Plus a stale `.env.bak` with the same secrets. Staging is correctly `600`.

## 🟠 A real data bug (pre-existing, not migration)

**No email has ever been sent** — 49/49 logged as "skipped" since July 8, because SMTP was never configured. Worse: the reminder job marks bookings as "reminded" **even when the send is skipped**. So **64 bookings can never receive a reminder**, even after you switch email on. Those are permanently burned unless we fix the logic and reset the flag.

## 🟠 Server-move landmines (for when you do move)
`domain-provisioner.sh` hardcodes this server's IP, so after a move studios' **custom domains would never provision** — site down, cron looking green. The backup bundle also misses custom-domain configs.

## 🟡 Smaller
`stg` isn't a reserved slug (a studio named that would get served staging's stale data); `HQ_PATH` is shared between live and staging; one studio's bogus custom domain (`lotus.com`) is polled every 5 min forever (288 DB writes/day, unbounded log); two retired certbot renewals will start erroring in September; no swap configured.

## ✅ Genuinely healthy
Certificates (renewal dry-runs pass, valid to Oct 20), **backups verified** (14 consecutive, contents validated), database intact (338 bookings, 149 orders), services stable, nginx valid, staging correctly isolated, TypeScript clean, no schema drift.

## ⚪ Not yours, but you should know
Your **SoulPilates GlitchTip** containers are in a crash loop — restarting every ~20s since a missing `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, ~7,000 restarts, now the dominant consumer of disk logs (`/var/log` at 1.3 GB). Untouched by me; worth passing to whoever owns that stack.

---

**Proposed fix order:**
1. 301-redirect the old revsports hostnames → `studionexis.com` *(fixes the wrong-app problem)*
2. Promote staging → live *(clears the docs, the mailer, and the 404 landmine)*
3. `chmod 600` the env files, delete the stale backup
4. Fix the reminder logic + reset the 64 burned flags
5. Server-move landmines, reserved `stg`, the polling loop

**Two things I need from you:** approval to **promote staging → live** (your workflow says I ask first), and confirmation you want the old domain **301-redirected** rather than switched fully dark.

I'd like to do #3 immediately regardless — that's a live secret exposure on a shared server.

## One blocker: I need a login

The public pages I can capture freely, but **~45 of the ~60 screens are behind login** (dashboard, schedule, clients, POS, payroll, settings, and the whole HQ portal). The old demo password from my notes is stale, and I was correctly blocked from resetting one myself — writing password hashes is exactly the kind of thing that *should* be blocked.

So I need you to either:
- **Give me a studio owner login** (staging is a nightly copy of live, so your normal live password works there), and ideally your **super-admin login** for the HQ screens; or

# create_new_file — Create a New Figma File

**MANDATORY: load this skill before every `create_new_file` tool call.** It encodes the plan-resolution decision tree, the editor-type contract, and the post-creation handoff to `use_figma`.

Use the `create_new_file` MCP tool to create a new blank Figma file in the user's drafts folder. This is typically used before `use_figma` when you need a fresh file to work with.

## Skill Arguments

This skill accepts optional arguments: `/figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName]`

- **editorType**: `design` (default), `figjam`, or `slides`
- **fileName**: Name for the new file (defaults to "Untitled")

Examples:
- `/figma-create-new-file` — creates a design file named "Untitled"
- `/figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard` — creates a FigJam file named "My Whiteboard"
- `/figma-create-new-file design My New Design` — creates a design file named "My New Design"
- `/figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review` — creates a Slides presentation named "Q3 Review"

Parse the arguments from the skill invocation. If editorType is not provided, default to `"design"`. If fileName is not provided, default to `"Untitled"`.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Resolve the planKey

The `create_new_file` tool requires a `planKey` parameter. Follow this decision tree:

1. **User already provided a planKey** (e.g. from a previous `whoami` call or in their prompt) → use it directly, skip to Step 2.

2. **No planKey available** → call the `whoami` tool. The response contains a `plans` array. Each plan has a `key`, `name`, `seat`, and `tier`.

   - **Single plan**: use its `key` field automatically.
   - **Multiple plans**: ask the user which team or organization they want to create the file in, then use the corresponding plan's `key`.

### Step 2: Call create_new_file

Call the `create_new_file` tool with:

| Parameter    | Required | Description |
|-------------|----------|-------------|
| `planKey`   | Yes      | The plan key from Step 1 |
| `fileName`  | Yes      | Name for the new file |
| `editorType`| Yes      | `"design"`, `"figjam"`, or `"slides"` |

Example:
```json
{
  "planKey": "team:123456",
  "fileName": "My New Design",
  "editorType": "design"
}
```

### Step 3: Use the result

The tool returns:
- `file_key` — the key of the newly created file
- `file_url` — a direct URL to open the file in Figma

Use the `file_key` for subsequent tool calls like `use_figma`.

## Important Notes

- The file is created in the user's **drafts folder** for the selected plan.
- Supported editor types are `"design"`, `"figjam"`, and `"slides"`.
- If `use_figma` is your next step, load the `figma-use` skill before calling it.

## Editor-specific notes

### Slides — newly created files have an empty grid

A `slides` file produced by this tool starts with **zero rows and zero slides** — `figma.getSlideGrid()` returns `[]`, not a default first slide. The page's only child is the `SLIDE_GRID` node itself, which is empty until you create content. The first call to `figma.createSlide()` implicitly creates row 0 and inserts the new slide there.

If your follow-up `use_figma` script assumes at least one slide exists (e.g. to read theme tokens off it), guard for the empty case or call `createSlide()` first. See [figma-use-slides → slide-grid](../figma-use-slides/references/slide-grid.md) for full details.

# Studio Nexis — UI screen capture (for Figma redesign)

**Figma file:** https://www.figma.com/design/mGaahl3K4nxcyHCfGM8zSB
**62 screens + 1 design-token sheet**, full-page, 1440px wide @ 2x retina.

## Staging demo logins (STAGING ONLY — never live)

| Role | URL | Email | Password |
|---|---|---|---|
| Studio owner | https://app.stg.studionexis.com | `demo.owner@studionexis.com` | `NexisDemo-2026!` |
| Super-admin (HQ) | https://hq.stg.studionexis.com | `demo.hq@studionexis.com` | `NexisDemo-2026!` |
| Instructor | https://app.stg.studionexis.com | `mia@dev-studio.com` | `NexisDemo-2026!` |

Created by `/opt/nexis/scripts/make-staging-demo-logins.mjs`, which **refuses to run**
unless `DATABASE_URL` points at `nexis_staging`. They sit on the `dev-studio` tenant,
which holds the demo dataset (41 clients / 338 bookings / 149 orders / 117 sessions).

> The 04:00 nightly sync rebuilds staging from live and **wipes these accounts**.
> Re-create them any time:
> ```
> cd /opt/nexis && DATABASE_URL="$(grep '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nexis-staging/.env | sed 's/^DATABASE_URL=//; s/"//g')" \
>   DEMO_PASS='NexisDemo-2026!' node scripts/make-staging-demo-logins.mjs
> ```

## Privacy
Client and staff records in staging were anonymised before capture (41 clients,
15 staff → fake names/emails/phones). **No real customer data is in these screens.**
Live was never touched. The nightly sync restores real data, so re-anonymise before
any future capture run.

## Re-running the capture
```
cd /opt/nexis-shots
export IDS_JSON="$(cat ids.json)" TENANT_SLUG=dev-studio
export OWNER_EMAIL=demo.owner@studionexis.com OWNER_PASS='NexisDemo-2026!'
export HQ_EMAIL=demo.hq@studionexis.com HQ_PASS='NexisDemo-2026!'
node capture.mjs        # -> out/*.png + out/manifest.json
```
`ids.json` holds real record ids so detail pages render populated, not empty.

| 1 · Public (marketing, login, signup, API docs) | 4 |
| 2 · Client booking site | 6 |
| 3 · Studio admin | 34 |
| 4 · HQ super-admin | 18 |
